content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early sessions, indicating a lag in adjusting to true market sentiment.", "Sentiment spikes near 1.00 correlate with sharp price corrections, suggesting model overconfidence in bullish signals.", "Model forecasts show mean-reversion bias, especially when true prices dip below 70.00, indicating underestimation of downside risk.", "High sentiment values (≥0.67) are followed by price corrections, implying sentiment-driven overshoots are not sustainable.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment is stable, suggesting models benefit from low volatility in sentiment signals.", "Models exhibit persistent upward bias in early forecast periods, suggesting a failure to account for recent price declines.", "True prices often reset after model forecast peaks, indicating a lag in model response to sentiment shifts.", "Sentiment reversal precedes price correction, suggesting models should adjust forecasts when sentiment drops below 0.33."]}
